newsitem.title: UK: Treasuries zigzag in London, more choppy times seen.
newsitem.headline: Treasuries zigzag in London, more choppy times seen.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries erased overnight gains and turned negative early on Monday in London before recovering to around late Friday levels, dealers said.
There were no major U.S. economic reports due on Monday.
But as the U.S. interest rate guessing game continued, analysts predicted more choppy trading leading up to some crucial economic reports later this week, including non-farm payroll data on Friday.
"The market's been rattled out of its complacency by a bevy of strong numbers over the holiday period," said Ian Amstad, senior economist at Bankers Trust in London.

"The markets are getting a little bit edgy going into the payroll number on Friday. So maybe the interest rate scenario isn't quite as benign as the market thought a couple of weeks ago," Amstad said. "Caution is the watchword."
The U.S. long bond at 1050 GMT was at 96-31 to yield 6.74 percent, compared with 97-04 late in Tokyo and 97-00 at the New York finish on Friday.
Two-year notes were at 99-21 bid, down a shade from 99-22 in Tokyo but up from 99-20 in New York, while five-years had eased to 99-13 from 99-15 in the Far East after finishing on Friday at 99-12.
As well as speculation about Federal Reserve policy, the market was preoccupied with the yen's fortunes and where Japanese capital flows were headed.
"There's still this obsession with what Japan is going to do," said Charles Quigley, salesman at Chase in London.
While the dollar has been charging higher against the yen recently there was a view that it was near the top of its range so this could limit yen-based investment in Treasuries, he said.
The dollar was at 115.85/90 yen, having risen to nearly the 117.00 level overnight. But Quigley added Japan was not necessarily the driving force for U.S. debt.
"In fact what domestic players decide to do with their money is a heck of a lot more important," he said.

He said the swaps market had generated demand in the two- to five-year sector of the curve, and added that as prices were back to around New York levels the market was now likely to mark time for a while.
The March T-bond future was at 111-19 in automated trade, up from 111-18 at the prior Chicago finish.
